about: Offline Horizons sanity references. All dynamics and numerical arithmetic are C++/WASM/native CSPICE; JavaScript and Python only orchestrate transport.

horizons.timeScale: UT is UTC after 1962, explicitly documented by each raw footer
horizons.hashConvention: sha256 is on-disk bytes. responseSha256 must equal raw/index.json sha256 using JSON.stringify(parsedRaw)+newline, reconstructing the original API response serialization exactly.

jwstPublishedExample.note: Read from the locally installed published crate; no network. Full rectangular sunshield area, nominal 6200 kg mass, Kapton proxy Cr=2-0.44=1.56. These are published assumptions, not measured 2026 JWST parameters.

publication.title: Park et al. (2021), The JPL Planetary and Lunar Ephemerides DE440 and DE441, AJ 161:105
publication.consulted: local repository attribution only; primary PDF not available offline

cause.statement: DE440 minus Horizons DE441, matching target 10 and Earth center 399, with FFM versus CSPICE UTC-to-TDB and single-JD rounding where applicable. SPICE removes the FFM clock/reader; its JD-parser control measures time-representation sensitivity. The remaining Horizons/CSPICE time-realization and ephemeris-coefficient contributions cannot be isolated without a local DE441 kernel.

bodies.toleranceRationale: Pre-existing docs/de440-validation.md cross-release smoke envelope: strict <10 m and <0.1 mm/s. Chosen before evaluating these rows; conservative modern lunar-model allowance, not a JPL accuracy guarantee or a published velocity bound. The separate <1 m question is reported without retuning.

cause.statement: Nominal hourly export epochs differ from the stored eight-decimal JD UTC TLIST; this adds a velocity-times-time displacement to the release residual.
Only the rounded-TLIST versus exact-hour time argument differs; both sides use the same CSPICE DE440.

bodies.note: Matched target 10 at the actual stored rounded UTC TLIST. The same-kernel and clock controls distinguish reader and timing effects from the cross-release comparison.

releaseAttribution.statement: Matching-target CSPICE DE440 minus Horizons DE441 reaches 0.8873397412330024 m and 0.00016713178096950526 mm/s over 50 epochs, within the unchanged 10 m / 0.1 mm/s envelope. Nominal-hour versus raw-TLIST epochs alone change DE440 positions by up to 8.450816691331209 m; changing only the CSPICE UTC input representation changes them by up to 0.6156250327328723 m and gives a 0.34376306934751644 m maximum Horizons residual. The matched-epoch residual combines target/Earth ephemeris release differences and unresolved Horizons/CSPICE time realization; these controls do not isolate DE441 coefficients. No local DE441 kernel is available to separate those contributions. No light-time, aberration or rotating-frame corrections are involved.

jwst.forceModel: Earth point mass (shared export GM) + Sun + Moon via exported DE440, with/without cannonball SRP; no maneuvers, drag, harmonics, relativity or planetary perturbations.
jwst.toleranceRationale: Preselected strict 10 km over 24 h: a loose order-of-magnitude sanity ceiling, not fitted to these residuals. C++ reports its equivalent constant acceleration and the nominal one-AU SRP displacement below. The bound allows several times a full-SRP modeling error, nominal/current mass and attitude/optics differences, plus small unmodeled corrections; an actual large maneuver could legitimately exceed it.

rows.note: Position-only strict <10 km sanity bound, preselected before evaluation; velocity is descriptive (null tolerance means no velocity gate). This is not an orbit-accuracy claim.

jwst.note: Horizons JWST_merged is a fitted, maneuver-corrected trajectory; neither run reproduces its OD/attitude/operational force model. The SRP-toggle displacement exceeds both reference residuals, demonstrating dominant sensitivity to the assumed optical force. This toggle does not identify every remaining error or establish an accurate spacecraft Cr.

verdict.statement: Sun/Moon exercise shipped FFM ephemeris; Venus and Jupiter system barycenter exercise independent CSPICE DE440 against the same Horizons targets. All four use the same 10 m / 0.1 mm/s bounds. JWST is a loose operational-trajectory sanity comparison. See measured rows and causes; no overall propagation-accuracy claim.

allocationEquivalence.statement: Release identity refreshed after all 72 reference cases at three settings returned byte-identical responses through the authenticated same-version pre-fix and released WASM. Numerical fields and unrelated pins are unchanged.
